name: HV 12203
description: A Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud that pulsates every 2.95 days; its mean radius is 24.8 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12203: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 24.8 +/- 1.4 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=LMC3750, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5750 +/- 125 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12203: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 44902.6 +/- 2481.8 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.06 +/- 0.004 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Large Magellanic Cloud that swells and shrinks every 3.0 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 24.8 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 44,903 parsecs away.

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.
No surface gravity averaged over the pulsation is published, only single-phase values, so no limb darkening is drawn.
Its distance is the Baade-Wesselink one its radius was measured at, so the Magellanic Cepheids spread a few kiloparsecs in depth.

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 4663635816857326976 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 10,000,000 of its distance per century
